brief: Pasquariello's weekly list of market developments. Memorial Day to Labor Day, cap-weighted S&P rose 4% and equal-weighted 7%, so the primary bull trend is intact, but index returns hid a momentum-factor unwind: the desk's TMT momentum pair printed its worst two months on record and has halved since June highs. Ahead is a catalyst-rich stretch: a possible 50 bps BOJ hike, the September FOMC, midterms, Hormuz warfare with European gas rising, UST buyback sizes Wednesday, PPI Thursday, a pivotal CPI Friday, ORCL earnings. Because the committee core is highly data dependent, this week's data seals next week's decision, though the house view is the Fed stays on hold. With the VIX just above YTD lows, options are not prohibitive, so his answer to both event risk and deteriorating debt math is to collect cheap convexity, and he notes this deficit episode, unlike late 2023, has not lifted rate volatility. Out of consensus: software beat NDX five straight weeks, private credit raised a record $99bn in Q2, fundamental long/short funds are up 14% YTD and systematic 17%, TPX up 12 of 13 sessions. He expects a choppy near term with neutral risk/reward, then a rally through year-end after the midterms.
